items.calibration: dropping in each run, before and after the capsule, a number of weighed specimens having a known heat content (generally silver specimens)
items.quote: The second instrument is a high temperature drop calorimeter. 4o It consists of two cells set one above the other, located inside ceramic and metallic tubes for thermal equalisation. The temperature difference between the two cells (working and reference cells) is measured by a 20-couple thermopile. The calorimeter is enclosed in a furnace which can be thermostatted at temperatures up to 1200°C. A typical run consists of dropping from a room temperature thermostat a small capsule containing about 2 g of a metal mixture. Subsequently, in a second run, the same capsule containing the reacted sample is dropped again into the calorimeter. The difference between the heat effects obtained in the two runs gives the room-temperature heat of formation of the alloy. The heat effects are evaluated by dropping in each run, before and after the capsule, a number of weighed specimens having a known heat content (generally silver specimens).

Differential thermal analysis was carried out (both on heating and on cooling) usually at rates between 2 and lO"C/min, using a model 404s Netzsch apparatus. This was performed both on as-cast and on annealed samples. The temperature accuracy, for the invariant equilibria, was estimated to be within f 1% of the measured value.
items.stated_uncertainty: within f 1% of the measured value

items.calibration: A cobalt standard was used for calibration in order to monitor beam current, gain and resolution of the spectrometer. Pure elements served as standards to carry out the deconvolution of overlapping peaks and background subtraction.
items.method: electron probe microanalysis based on energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy
items.quote: In a few cases a quantitative electron probe microanalysis based on energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (Si(Li) detector) was used to check the phase compositions. The samples were analysed employing an acceleration voltage of 20 kV for a counting time of 100s. X-ray energy spectra were processed using the ZAF4/FLS software package supplied by Link Systems Ltd. A cobalt standard was used for calibration in order to monitor beam current, gain and resolution of the spectrometer. Pure elements served as standards to carry out the deconvolution of overlapping peaks and background subtraction. Finally, the X-ray intensities were corrected for ZAF effects using the TIM1 program.

items.calibration: addition of a calibration standard (Si) to the sample
items.quote: The X-ray examination was carried out on powder samples using either the Debye method (with Cu K, or Fe K, filtered radiations, applying to the d values the Nelson-Riley correction function and computing and refining the lattice parameters through a least-square interpolation) or a vertical diffractometer with Cu K, radiation. In this last case the addition of a calibration standard (Si) to the sample was made to achieve higher accuracy in the measurements of the d values.

items.label: All the samples
items.quote: All the samples were prepared starting from Al and R metals with nominal purity of 99.999 and 99.9 mass%, respectively.
For the thermochemical measurements, on the other hand, the samples were prepared directly inside the calorimeter itself.
items.synthesis: prepared directly inside the calorimeter itself

items.label: Alrich alloys
items.quote: To avoid side reactions with tantalum, the Alrich alloys were prepared in an induction furnace by melting pieces of the constituent metals in alumina crucibles, under an argon atmosphere.
items.synthesis: prepared in an induction furnace by melting pieces of the constituent metals in alumina crucibles, under an argon atmosphere
